title: Regulated Deployments: Negotiation Cheat Sheet (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Quick reference for sales + solutions when negotiating Private (VPC/on-prem) deals with regulated customers. Focus: control plane language, risk framing, and specific negotiation levers we can offer without opening up product or compliance roadmaps. Draft — intentionally concise so SEs can memorize scripts.

Audience:
- Sales AE / AMs handling procurement
- Solutions / SEs supporting security and infra review
- Legal for redlines and SLA asks

One-line positioning to lead with (exec summary):
- "We provide a private deployment model that separates data plane from our optional control plane, supports customer-managed keys and networking, and is backed by a hardened audit and support SLA — so your regulated workloads stay inside your network and you keep operational control."

Control plane language (what to say, and what to avoid):
- Say: "Customer-managed data plane + optional control plane with constrained metadata exchange. Control plane handles orchestration, telemetry, and billing."
- Prefer: "optional / opt-in control plane" and "metadata-only interactions" rather than "managed service with access to customer data".
- Emphasize: "We do not persist customer payloads in the control plane. All models and inference data remain in your VPC when you choose private."
- Avoid: "full stack access", "we need to see the data to optimize performance". If asked, reframe: "We can run diagnostic tooling as a one-time, audited operation under an agreed scope."

Data flow plain-language snippet (for security reviews):
- "Inference requests and model artifacts live inside your VPC (data plane). The control plane only receives hashed job metadata and health telemetry (no unencrypted prompt/response bodies). We support KMS-wrapped keys for any secret exchange. If you require zero control-plane metadata, we can offer an air-gapped installer variant."

Buyer personas & short scripts
- CISO / Head of Security:
  - Concern: Data exfiltration, vendor insider access.
  - Script: "We support envelope encryption with your KMS and restrict the control plane to metadata-only telemetry. We provide audit logs and an HSM/KMS integration scope for your security team to validate."
- Platform / Infra Eng:
  - Concern: Networking, observability, lifecycle ops.
  - Script: "Deployment uses your subnets, supports private endpoints, and we supply a sidecar for local metrics to feed your observability stack. Rollouts can be pinned to a model version and controlled via feature-flag style policies."
- Procurement / Legal:
  - Concern: SLA, liability, termination/data return.
  - Script: "We include a data return/export clause, a 30/90 day audit window, and options for extended log retention under an add-on. For regulated customers we commit to a 99.9% control-plane availability SLA and an agreed RTO for on-prem critical failures."

Top buyer objections & rebuttals (short):
- "You need access to our data to troubleshoot." -> Rebuttal: "We run scoped, auditable debug sessions with customer approval; we can share exact logs and hashes for triage without sharing payloads."
- "Control plane is a risk surface." -> Rebuttal: "We treat it as thin orchestration: minimum metadata, KMS integration, and optional private-control-plane deployment."
- "We can host ourselves — why pay?" -> Rebuttal: "Self-hosting requires full lifecycle ownership (patching, model upgrades, kernel/quantization tuning). Our private option offloads that operational burden while keeping data inside your boundary; we offer migration/runbook support for hybrid transitions."

Negotiation levers (what sales can offer quickly):
- Technical acceptance criteria: agreed checklist (KMS integration, private endpoints, audit log format) signed as appendix.
- Support tier swap: elevated SLAs + named SEs for a contract period (30–90 days) as concession.
- Pilot terms: limited commit with option to extend at pre-agreed pricing if pilot metrics met.
- On-prem installer + 6 months managed ops as a short-term concession for big regulated deals.
- Data residency clause + guaranteed log retention policy for an add-on fee.

Pricing concession templates (to avoid giving blanket discounts):
- "We can offer a one-time onboarding credit (X hours of SE time) in exchange for a 12-month minimum term."
- "For multi-year commitments we can tier down per-inference pricing but keep a minimum support retainer."

Security checklist for intake (put this into initial SOW appendix):
- KMS/HSM integration path defined (customer KMS preferred)
- Private endpoints and VPC peering or PrivateLink
- RBAC and least-privilege service accounts with short TTLs
- Audit log schema + retention agreed (ISO/SOC needs)
- Vulnerability scanning cadence and patch policy for the runtime
- Option for penetration test / firewall rule review on a cadence

Competitive notes (quick summary & counterplays)
- Competitor A (managed-first provider): claims "no infra burden". Counter: "We match operational simplicity while offering private topology and stronger KMS controls."
- Competitor B (OSS self-hosted runtime): claims "full control, lower cost". Counter: "Self-hosting shifts ongoing model-ops, kernel tuning, and quantization efforts to the customer — we include model performance tuning and regressions monitoring as part of dedicated/private packages."
- Competitor C (cloud vendor): claims "deep compliance pedigree". Counter: "We provide the same compliance integrations and can sign enterprise SLAs; our differentiated point is inference economics and rollout controls across variants."

Legal redline hotspots to expect
- Access to incident data: push to scoped, timeboxed forensic access rather than blanket access.
- Data deletion certification: offer a deletion audit and certificate as part of termination.
- Subprocessor list: provide standard list and a notification cadence for additions.

Example email snippet for procurement/legal (short):
"Hi [Name],
Thanks — attached is our standard private-deploy appendix with the KMS + audit log requirements called out. For compliance clarity: we treat the control plane as orchestration-only (no persisted payloads) and we will sign a scoped access appendix for any troubleshooting. Happy to schedule a 30-minute meeting with our security lead to walk the SOW appendix."

Operational TODOs (notes to SEs & solutions):
- Create a one-page KMS integration diagram (customer KMS -> data plane -> control plane hashed metadata), attach to SOW.
- Draft a short test plan for security teams: what logs/fields we will provide during acceptance testing.
- Compile list of past deals with similar concessions and outcomes (for pricing playbook).

Open questions / escalation items:
- What is the maximum metadata we can commit to zero-ing out in the control plane without breaking observability for customers? (SEs: test a pinned build)
- For very large regulated customers, do we want a documented runbook for complete on-prem fallback (customer-run runtime) as a paid service?

Appendix (quick checklist for demo call)
- Lead with data residency and KMS
- Show a short diagram of control vs data plane separation
- Have the KMS integration flow and RBAC example ready
- Offer the onboarding credit or SE time rather than price cuts

— end of draft —
Notes: keep this doc short and portable. We should convert into a 1-pager and a separate technical appendix that SEs can attach during procurement reviews.
